headline: ANDINA COPPER ANDC COBRASCO CDH010 COLOMBIA: 264m AT 0.63% CU WITHIN 504m AT 0.48% CU — PORPHYRY FOOTPRINT NOW 1.2km, OPEN ALL DIRECTIONS
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Andina Copper Corporation (TSX-V: ANDC)
snippet: Andina Copper Corporation (TSX-V: ANDC) released August 11, 2026 assay results from hole CDH010 at the Cobrasco Porphyry Copper-Moly Discovery in Chocó, Colombia, intersecting a strongly mineralized upper interval commencing at 36m and extending to 540m downhole. The highlight interval of 264m at 0.63% copper is nested within a broader 504m intersection at 0.48% copper — an unusually wide intercept for a porphyry system at this stage. The drill-defined footprint now measures approximately 1,200m x 550–700m and remains open in all directions, with results from CDH011 imminent and drilling underway from a new platform 350m to the northwest. Wide, high-grade porphyry systems of this scale in a Colombian copper-moly terrane attract M&A attention from producers seeking reserve replacement; the Cobrasco footprint rivals the early-stage geometry of several Latin American juniors that progressed from first assays to acquisition within 24–36 months. At current copper above $6.60/lb, the economics underpinning a porphyry of Cobrasco's emerging scale have materially shifted compared with 2022 feasibility benchmarks.

headline: LAKE VICTORIA GOLD LVG TEMBO TANZANIA: MAIDEN 480,100 OZ INFERRED + 99,700 OZ INDICATED — ADJACENT TO BARRICK'S BULYANHULU MINE
source_name: StockTitan / Lake Victoria Gold Ltd. (TSX-V: LVG)
snippet: Lake Victoria Gold Ltd. (TSX-V: LVG) announced August 11, 2026 a maiden NI 43-101 Mineral Resource Estimate for the Tembo Gold Project in northwestern Tanzania: an Inferred Resource of 13.33 million tonnes at 1.12 g/t gold for 480,100 ounces and an Indicated Resource of 2.69 million tonnes at 1.16 g/t gold for 99,700 ounces — combined first resource of approximately 580,000 ounces. Tembo is located directly adjacent to Barrick Gold's Bulyanhulu Mine, one of Africa's highest-grade underground gold operations at over 15 million ounces. Geological continuity of the Bulyanhulu structure across the licence boundary into Tembo, combined with Barrick's established infrastructure corridor in the district, makes Tembo a logistically advantaged development target compared with remote Tanzanian projects. A 580,000-ounce maiden resource adjacent to a producing Barrick mine — in a district where Barrick has historically consolidated prospective ground — is the type of announcement that draws acquisition consideration at current gold prices above $4,400/oz.

headline: COPPER HOLDS $6.65/LB AS DRC EXPORT BAN, US TARIFF WAREHOUSING AND CHILEAN MINE WOES COLLIDE — ALL-TIME HIGH $6.77 SET LAST WEEK
snippet: COMEX copper held at $6.65 per pound on August 11, 2026, consolidating below the August 7 all-time record of $6.77/lb — a rally driven by three overlapping supply shocks converging simultaneously: (1) The DRC publicly announced August 6 it is banning copper and cobalt concentrate exports effective June 29 to force domestic smelting, echoing Indonesia's 2014 nickel ore playbook; (2) US import tariff uncertainty continues to redirect metal from international markets into American warehouses, tightening LME inventories; (3) Operational disruptions at Chilean copper mines — the world's largest copper producer — have constrained concentrate output. Goldman Sachs notes the DRC concentrate volume is relatively small in global terms (DRC exported only ~54,000t of copper concentrate in Q1 2026 vs 696,000t of refined cathodes), but the policy signal of another major supplier restricting raw exports is consistent with structural resource nationalism across the copper supply chain. For TSX-V copper developers, sustained copper above $6.50/lb materially improves project NPVs and financing terms compared with the $4.50–$5.00 range that defined project economics in 2022–2023.

headline: NEXGOLD NEXG GOLDBORO NOVA SCOTIA: 108.76 g/t Au OVER 1.40m, 67.23 g/t Au OVER 2.20m IN OPEN PIT INFILL — UPDATED FS DUE Q3 2026
snippet: NexGold Mining Corp. (TSX-V: NEXG) released additional high-grade assay results August 11, 2026 from its 40,000m reverse circulation infill drill program at the Goldboro Gold Project in Nova Scotia, with hole BR-25-578 returning 108.76 g/t gold over 1.40 metres (including 304.00 g/t over 0.50m) and a second hole delivering 67.23 g/t gold over 2.20 metres — both within the open pit Mineral Resource area. NexGold expanded the program from 30,000m to 40,000m based on consistent high-grade intercept continuity; an updated Feasibility Study is targeted Q3 2026. High-grade infill drilling in a near-development project upgrades Inferred and Indicated ounces to Measured and validates grade continuity underpinning the FS mine schedule. At gold above $4,400/oz, Goldboro's Nova Scotia location and established infrastructure corridor make it one of the most near-term development-stage gold projects in Atlantic Canada — a jurisdiction with no permitting moratorium and growing federal support for domestic gold production.

headline: GETTY COPPER GTC HIGHLAND VALLEY BC: 194m AT 0.62% CU FROM 27m — SPRING PROGRAM COMPLETES 10,807m, FALL DRILL STARTS OCTOBER
source_name: Investing News Network / Getty Copper Inc. (TSX-V: GTC)
snippet: Getty Copper Inc. (TSX-V: GTC) released a second batch of assay results from the Getty North porphyry copper deposit on August 11, 2026, with highlights including 194 metres at 0.62% copper from 27 metres depth — solid near-surface grade for a porphyry at this stage. The 2026 spring program at the Getty Project in BC's Highland Valley Copper Camp totalled 10,807 metres across multiple holes, exceeding the initial 8,000–10,000m budget within the same cost envelope due to lower-than-budgeted drilling costs. Expansion drilling has extended Getty North mineralization by over 60 metres, now more than 230 metres beyond historical holes across three cross-sections. A fall program starts October. Getty North sits in the same BC geological camp as Teck Resources' Highland Valley Copper Mine (100,000 t/day capacity) — a proximity that provides geological validation and potential future logistical advantages. Near-surface porphyry grades of 0.62% Cu in this district, with copper above $6.60/lb, change the project economics conversation entirely from where it stood 24 months ago.

headline: MP MATERIALS Q2: REVENUE +89% TO $108M, NdPr VOLUME +277% — FIRST GM MAGNET SHIPMENTS Q4 2026, STOCK UP 24% IN WEEK
source_name: Yahoo Finance / MP Materials Corp. (NYSE: MP)
snippet: MP Materials Corp. (NYSE: MP) reported Q2 FY2026 results August 6 that drove shares up 24% over the following week to $54.56 as of August 10: revenue of $108.49 million (up 89% year-over-year, beating consensus by 13%), with NdPr oxide and metal sales surging 277% to $94.43 million on 1,006 metric tonnes of separated product volume. Q3 guidance projects NdPr production above 1,000 MT at realized pricing in the high $90s per kilogram. First commercial magnet shipments to General Motors are expected in Q4 2026 — completing MP's transformation from a concentrate-only miner into a fully integrated US rare earth magnet producer, a milestone no other Western company has reached at scale. Needham raised its price target following results, citing a nine-figure gadolinium supply agreement with a US aerospace and defense customer as evidence that government-backed domestic rare earth supply chains are transitioning from policy aspiration to commercial reality.

headline: AMERICA CONSUMED 50 MILLION POUNDS OF URANIUM IN 2024 — AND PRODUCED JUST 677,000
snippet: A market commentary published August 10, 2026 on GlobeNewswire quantified the structural gap at the core of the US uranium investment thesis: American nuclear reactors consumed approximately 50 million pounds of uranium equivalent in 2024 while domestic US mines produced just 677,000 pounds — a 74:1 consumption-to-production ratio leaving the US dependent on imports for 98.6% of its nuclear fuel needs. US reactor demand is set to grow as the federal government's $80 billion nuclear commitment comes online and AI data centre power demand drives new reactor construction approvals. Against this backdrop, uranium producers with US-based assets — including Uranium Energy's recently acquired Wyoming operations (up to 12.1 million lbs/yr potential capacity) and Peninsula Energy's Lance Project in Wyoming — are positioned in a contracting market where Western utilities are actively seeking domestic and allied-nation supply alternatives to Russian and Chinese-linked producers.

headline: US URANIUM CONTRACTING WAVE IS COMING — EAGLE NUCLEAR CEO CITES Q2 RECORD 258,745 LBS OUTPUT AND NEAR $1B LIQUIDITY
snippet: Eagle Nuclear Energy's CEO told Mining.com that US nuclear utilities are approaching an inflection point that could trigger a new wave of uranium supply contracting — a cycle that historically drives 12–24 month advances in spot and long-term uranium prices as utilities lock in multi-year supply. Eagle Nuclear added to the Solactive Global Uranium Index in August (bringing passive ETF buying) reported Q2 2026 record output of 258,745 pounds of U3O8 at a 57% uranium gross margin, with close to $1 billion in liquidity. The CEO's contracting wave thesis is grounded in utility procurement cycles: US reactors historically re-enter the spot and contract market 18–24 months before fuel assembly deliveries are needed; with new reactor capacity coming online in 2027–2028, the contracting window logically opens mid-2026 through 2027. For junior uranium developers on the TSX-V and ASX, utility contracting activity is the single most important price-support mechanism for project financing — a new contract cycle would validate development timelines and materially expand the pool of patient institutional capital willing to fund pre-production uranium assets.

headline: MALAYSIA MULLS CONDITIONAL EASING OF RAW RARE EARTH EXPORT BAN — US, AUSTRALIA, FRANCE, INDIA PUSH HARD AS CHINA TIGHTENS GRIP
snippet: Malaysia is weighing a conditional relaxation of its 2024 moratorium on raw rare earth exports, with the government reviewing whether to allow processed or semi-processed rare earth exports under conditions requiring foreign investment commitments and technology transfer to develop domestic processing capability. The policy review comes after China tightened heavy rare earth export controls in 2025, intensifying Western supply chain pressure and drawing active lobbying from the US, Australia, France, and India. Any easing would be conditional rather than open — mirroring Indonesia's tiered approach to nickel export policy — meaning raw ore shipments would remain banned, but value-added concentrates and separated materials could be permitted. Malaysia holds significant rare earth deposits in Sarawak and Pahang and is one of the few non-Chinese sources of heavy rare earth materials capable of supplying the quantities needed by Western defense and clean energy industries. A conditional Malaysian opening would mark the first meaningful expansion of the Western rare earth supply base since MP Materials separated its first 1,000 tonnes of NdPr.

headline: PAN AMERICAN SILVER PAAS Q2 RESULTS TOMORROW — $1.16B REVENUE (+43%) AND +93% EPS EXPECTED AS SILVER RALLY FLOWS THROUGH FINANCIALS
snippet: Pan American Silver Corp. (TSX: PAAS) reports Q2 2026 results August 12 before market open, with analyst consensus projecting $1.16 billion in revenue (up 43.2% year-on-year) and earnings per share of $0.84 (up 93.4% year-on-year), driven by an estimated 6.5 million ounces of silver production (up 27.1% year-over-year) at prices well above $65/oz. Silver has continued to trade above $65 in August, providing margin conditions not seen in the sector since 2011. Investors are leaning into PAAS ahead of results; the combination of operational leverage, production growth, and structurally higher silver prices creates an earnings setup the market has not priced in a decade. The PAAS print will set the sentiment tone for silver producer earnings across the sector and likely influence trading in First Majestic (FR/AG), Endeavour Silver, Silvercorp, and other silver-leveraged TSX names through the rest of the week.

headline: GOLD MINERS IN LOW-TEENS P/E WITH RECORD MARGINS — SECTOR TEEING UP FOR EQUITY RE-RATING, SAYS VANECK SWOT
snippet: VanEck's weekly Gold SWOT analysis, published on GoldSeek, highlights that gold mining stocks are generating near-record Q2 2026 profits — Agnico Eagle alone reported $1.33 billion in free cash flow in Q2 at a realized gold price of $4,483/oz with AISC of just $1,459/oz, and returned $625 million to shareholders — while the sector P/E ratio remains in the low-to-mid teens, a significant valuation discount to historical mining multiples and the broader S&P 500. The SWOT identifies the core opportunity: institutional capital has flowed primarily into physical gold (GLD, PHYS) and streaming/royalty companies rather than pure mining producers, meaning the re-rating to reflect record profitability has only partially occurred. The setup historically precedes a catch-up move in mining equities relative to bullion — as seen in 2016 and 2020 when gold mining stocks outperformed the gold price by 40–80% during the re-rating phase. For retail investors already positioned in junior mining exploration companies, strong senior producer earnings provide macro legitimacy for continued junior market momentum, as the junior sector typically re-rates 6–12 months after seniors confirm a new earnings regime.
